definition: A mature gamma-delta T cell whose T cell receptor does NOT use the Vδ2 (TRDV2) delta variable segment. This grouping is dominated by Vδ1 (TRDV1)-expressing cells, with smaller Vδ3/Vδ5 contributions, and is tissue-associated (enriched in epithelial and mucosal sites and secondary lymphoid tissue) in contrast to the blood-dominant Vγ9Vδ2 subset. It exhibits cytotoxic effector capacity and recognises stress-induced and non-classical MHC-like ligands in a butyrophilin/phosphoantigen-independent manner. The existing V1delta gamma-delta T cell (CL:0020001) is its principal subtype. It is defined by the absence of Vδ2 (TRDV2) T cell receptor usage.

logical_axioms.notes: gamma-delta T cells of this subset exert perforin/granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity.

references.supports: Upstream tonsil single-cell study used as a starting annotation by the reference atlas.

Review that establishes the Vδ2 vs non-Vδ2 dichotomy of human γδ T cells. Non-Vδ2 cells (predominantly Vδ1) are defined by NOT using the Vδ2 element; they are rare in blood but enriched in mucosal tissues and skin, and recognise stress-associated surface antigens. Markers here are at the protein/TCR level (Vδ element usage), the surface correlate of the atlas TRDV2-negative / TRDV1 transcript signature.

Review contrasting innate-like Vγ9Vδ2 cells with the heterogeneous Vδ2− subset. States that Vδ2− γδ T cells preferentially reside in epithelial tissues and mainly comprise Vδ1+ cells, with fewer Vδ3+/Vδ5+; their TCR repertoire narrows with age and expands with CMV. Protein/TCR-level subset definition.

Primary study directly linking TRANSCRIPT-level TRDV1/TRDV2 to the Vδ1/Vδ2 protein subsets. In non-malignant lung tissue TRDV1 (Vδ1) transcript exceeds TRDV2 (Vδ2), matching flow-cytometric protein data, and tissue Vδ1 cells adopt a CD103+ tissue-resident memory phenotype. This is the key bridge between the atlas's TRDV2-negative/TRDV1 transcript label and the protein-defined non-Vδ2/Vδ1 subset.

Classic immunohistology study establishing that human γδ TCR+ lymphocytes populate organized lymphoid tissues including the tonsil, at frequencies similar to other lymphoid organs and without epithelial tropism. Provides direct evidence that γδ T cells (of which the non-Vδ2/Vδ1 subset is a part) are resident in the tonsil. Protein/antibody (anti-TCR-delta) level.

Review defining the non-Vδ2 γδ-TCR compartment as Vδ1 plus Vδ3, mostly tissue-resident in barrier epithelium, with Vδ1 the most abundant and recognising CD1/MR1-presented and stress-induced ligands. Protein/TCR-level definition; corroborates that 'non-Vδ2' is not a single clonotype but a compartment dominated by Vδ1.

Review confirming that human γδ T cells are grouped into Vδ2 and non-Vδ2 subsets with distinct biology, and that tissue residency segregates by subset: Vγ9Vδ2 predominate in blood while non-Vδ2 γδ T reside in barrier tissues. Explicitly notes γδ T cells are identified by TCR delta chain usage (protein level).

Study noting γδ T cells are abundant in mucosal lymphoid tissue (up to ~50% of T cells there); the Vδ1+ subset is mainly situated at mucosal sites and responds to stress-induced non-classical MHC molecules MICA/MICB, in contrast to the blood-dominant phosphoantigen-reactive Vγ9Vδ2 subset. Protein/TCR-level definition.
Azimuth human_tonsil_v2 single-cell reference atlas (source of the cell-type annotation).

justification: Defined by ABSENCE of Vδ2/TRDV2 — the negative criterion is stated in the definition text and is NOT asserted as a logical axiom (no positive marker for an absent feature). Parent CL:0000800; the existing CL:0020001 (V1delta gamma-delta T cell) should be reclassified as a subtype of this term. Species-neutral.

## New term request: non-Vdelta2 gamma-delta T cell

**Proposed label:** non-Vdelta2 gamma-delta T cell

**Definition:** A mature gamma-delta T cell whose T cell receptor does NOT use the Vδ2 (TRDV2) delta variable segment. This grouping is dominated by Vδ1 (TRDV1)-expressing cells, with smaller Vδ3/Vδ5 contributions, and is tissue-associated (enriched in epithelial and mucosal sites and secondary lymphoid tissue) in contrast to the blood-dominant Vγ9Vδ2 subset. It exhibits cytotoxic effector capacity and recognises stress-induced and non-classical MHC-like ligands in a butyrophilin/phosphoantigen-independent manner. The existing V1delta gamma-delta T cell (CL:0020001) is its principal subtype. It is defined by the absence of Vδ2 (TRDV2) T cell receptor usage.

**Parent (is_a):** mature gamma-delta T cell (CL:0000800)

**Anatomical location:** lymphoid tissue (UBERON:0001744)

**Logical axioms:**
- `capable of` (RO:0002215) some **T cell mediated cytotoxicity** (GO:0001913) — gamma-delta T cells of this subset exert perforin/granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity.

**Synonyms:**
- non-TRDV2 gamma-delta T cell (exact)
- non-Vδ2 gamma-delta T cell (exact)
- Vdelta1-enriched gamma-delta T cell (related)

**References:**
- King et al. (2021). DOI: 10.1126/sciimmunol.abh3768 ; PMID:34623901 — Source single-cell atlas (Azimuth human_tonsil_v2).
- Kabelitz et al. (2013). DOI: 10.4161/onci.23304 ; PMID:23802074 — Review that establishes the Vδ2 vs non-Vδ2 dichotomy of human γδ T cells. Non-Vδ2 cells (predominantly Vδ1) are defined by NOT using the Vδ2 element; they are rare in blood but enriched in mucosal tissues and skin, and recognise stress-associated surface antigens. Markers here are at the protein/TCR level (Vδ element usage), the surface correlate of the atlas TRDV2-negative / TRDV1 transcript signature.
- Khairallah et al. (2018). DOI: 10.3389/fimmu.2018.02636 ; PMID:30538697 — Review contrasting innate-like Vγ9Vδ2 cells with the heterogeneous Vδ2− subset. States that Vδ2− γδ T cells preferentially reside in epithelial tissues and mainly comprise Vδ1+ cells, with fewer Vδ3+/Vδ5+; their TCR repertoire narrows with age and expands with CMV. Protein/TCR-level subset definition.
- Wu et al. (2022). DOI: 10.1038/s43018-022-00376-z ; PMID:35637401 — Primary study directly linking TRANSCRIPT-level TRDV1/TRDV2 to the Vδ1/Vδ2 protein subsets. In non-malignant lung tissue TRDV1 (Vδ1) transcript exceeds TRDV2 (Vδ2), matching flow-cytometric protein data, and tissue Vδ1 cells adopt a CD103+ tissue-resident memory phenotype. This is the key bridge between the atlas's TRDV2-negative/TRDV1 transcript label and the protein-defined non-Vδ2/Vδ1 subset.
- Groh et al. (1989). DOI: 10.1084/jem.169.4.1277 ; PMID:2564416 — Classic immunohistology study establishing that human γδ TCR+ lymphocytes populate organized lymphoid tissues including the tonsil, at frequencies similar to other lymphoid organs and without epithelial tropism. Provides direct evidence that γδ T cells (of which the non-Vδ2/Vδ1 subset is a part) are resident in the tonsil. Protein/antibody (anti-TCR-delta) level.
- Pérez et al. (2020). DOI: 10.3389/fimmu.2020.583716 ; PMID:33262761 — Review defining the non-Vδ2 γδ-TCR compartment as Vδ1 plus Vδ3, mostly tissue-resident in barrier epithelium, with Vδ1 the most abundant and recognising CD1/MR1-presented and stress-induced ligands. Protein/TCR-level definition; corroborates that 'non-Vδ2' is not a single clonotype but a compartment dominated by Vδ1.
- Fisher et al. (2026). DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-73451-z ; PMID:42173864 — Review confirming that human γδ T cells are grouped into Vδ2 and non-Vδ2 subsets with distinct biology, and that tissue residency segregates by subset: Vγ9Vδ2 predominate in blood while non-Vδ2 γδ T reside in barrier tissues. Explicitly notes γδ T cells are identified by TCR delta chain usage (protein level).
- Negash et al. (2018). DOI: 10.1186/s12879-018-3361-9 ; PMID:30219039 — Study noting γδ T cells are abundant in mucosal lymphoid tissue (up to ~50% of T cells there); the Vδ1+ subset is mainly situated at mucosal sites and responds to stress-induced non-classical MHC molecules MICA/MICB, in contrast to the blood-dominant phosphoantigen-reactive Vγ9Vδ2 subset. Protein/TCR-level definition.

**Justification:** Defined by ABSENCE of Vδ2/TRDV2 — the negative criterion is stated in the definition text and is NOT asserted as a logical axiom (no positive marker for an absent feature). Parent CL:0000800; the existing CL:0020001 (V1delta gamma-delta T cell) should be reclassified as a subtype of this term. Species-neutral.
